name: Chord Clock
description: Each key starts as a soft pulse at its pitch slowed by whole octaves, quickens into its tone, and leaves the chord's own polyrhythm circling underneath.

params.name: Pulse
params.description: What one pulse is made of. The tone is the same pulse at full speed, so this changes both: round, pure, reedy, airy, or bright and dying.

params.name: Body
params.description: What the pulses strike and the tone is heard through: a bar over a box, ringing glass, a deep membrane, or a column of air with vowels in it.

params.name: Path
params.description: How a held key goes between rhythm and tone: it quickens smoothly, climbs octave by octave, starts as tone and slows down, or goes and returns.

params.name: Slowness
params.description: How far below its pitch a key's pulse runs. Near fusion it purrs, in the middle it patters, and at the slow end single pulses fall seconds apart.

params.name: Quicken
params.description: How long a key takes along its Path, from pulse to tone or the other way round. On There and back it is the time of one whole round.

params.name: Ratios
params.description: Which numbers keys make with the lowest key: threes, then fives, sevens, nines, elevens. It sets tuning and rhythm, and plain ratios sound brighter.

params.name: Agree
params.description: How far keys are drawn to exact ratios with the lowest key. Fully drawn, the whole pattern returns. With less, pitches stay tempered and the pattern drifts.

params.name: Tone
params.description: How loud and open the tone is, which is the pulse at full speed. At zero only the rhythm is left.

params.name: Rhythm
params.description: How loud the pulses are, both the ones that quicken and the slow ones that go on circling under the tone.

params.name: Bloom
params.description: How much the tone waits for the pulses to join. At zero it stands from the start; at the top it grows out of them and turns bright as they fuse.

params.name: Lift
params.description: How much each pulse lifts the tone of its key, in level and colour. At the top the tone comes only with the pulses.

params.name: Lower octaves
params.description: How much of the pulses at half and a quarter of the pitch is in the tone while it comes together. Past a quarter some stays for good, darker and deeper.

params.name: Pulse width
params.description: How long each pulse is. Narrow is hard and bright in the pulses and in the tone; wide is soft and dark.

params.name: Damping
params.description: How soon the body stops, after a pulse and after a key, and how little it colours the tone. Low rings on and resonates; high leaves dry knocks.

params.name: Accent
params.description: How much the pulse is stressed where a key's clock comes back together with the lowest key's. A key alone is stressed every fourth pulse.

params.name: Stagger
params.description: Moves the keys' clocks apart, so that their pulses answer each other in turn and do not fall together on the return.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long the tone takes to come in. Short is a stroke that starts bright and settles; long is a swell. The first pulse always falls at once.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long tone and pulses take to fade after a key is let go.

params.name: Slow again
params.description: How much the pulses slow down and stay behind when a key is let go, like a clock running out.

params.name: Velocity
params.description: How much playing harder makes a key louder, its pulses harder and its tone brighter.

params.name: Width
params.description: How wide the harmonics and the body's ringing are placed, and how far they wander between the sides.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. The tone is a moving band-limited table of four periods made by one transform for both ears, the pulses excite a modal body, and both run from one master clock whose ratios are the chord's. Ratios of bodies are those of bars, glasses, membranes and pipes; levels are voiced by measurement.
